summary.headline: Capacite Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR712 crores, with EBITDA up 27% to INR109 crores at a 15.3% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6% YoY to INR712 crores and EBITDA rose 27% to INR109 crores, with margin expanding to 15.3% from 12.8%. PAT fell to INR45 crores from INR53 crores as other income dropped to INR1.5 crores from INR33.5 crores. FY26 order inflow was INR4,446 crores, above the INR3,500 crore guidance, and working capital days fell 43 days. Management attributed the weak revenue growth to labour shortfall after West Bengal and assembly elections, and flagged commodity-driven escalation lag, with an INR10 crore provision and a margin guidance cut to 15.5-16.5% for FY27.

segments.name: Public sector (order book and revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Public sector is 57% of the standalone order book of INR13,498 crores as on 31 March 2026. Management later said the revenue mix is about 60-65% public and 32-35% private.

segments.name: Private sector
segments.commentary: Private sector is 43% of the order book. Management said NCR private order backlog is about INR1,500 crores and NBCC public backlog in NCR is about INR800 crores.

segments.name: CIDCO and MHADA
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was about INR223.68 crores from MHADA and close to INR400 crores from CIDCO. FY27 guidance is INR350-400 crores for MHADA and INR500-600 crores for CIDCO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 15.5-16.5% due to commodity inflation; if global uncertainty eases within a couple of months, guidance is restored to 16.5-17.5%.
FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance of about 20% year on year, backed by the order book.
FY27 order inflow guidance of INR4,500-5,000 crores; management expects about INR1,000 crores each in Q1 and Q2 and INR2,500-3,000 crores in H2.
FY27 finance cost to fall by INR6-8 crores in absolute terms; net working capital target of 56-60 days over the next 8 quarters.
FY27 capex target of about INR165 crores, mainly aluminium formwork and jump-form; non-core asset sales target of INR50 crores (about INR90 crores remaining to be sold over about 24 months).
FY27 other income expected at INR3-4 crores per quarter, plus or minus 10%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex additions were INR147.33 crores, including INR67.81 crores in Q4 FY26.
FY27 capex target is about INR165 crores, mainly aluminium formwork and jump-form.

Labour: average requirement is about 14,000+ workers versus about 11,000 currently, with a peak of about 9,000 in March and part of April; about 3,000 short across 30 project sites, with recovery expected by end-May.
Net turnover ratio of core assets was 5.2x in FY26, in line with FY25; management expects execution to improve this.
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow was INR4,446 crores, above the INR3,500 crore guidance; management said it has bid more than INR5,000 crores and is negotiating about INR1,000 crores with existing clients.

Electrical and aluminium product prices rose about 18-20% from February to April 2026, while the WPI-linked escalation was only about 8% and about 2% in Feb-Mar; the company booked a INR10 crore provision in construction expenses in Q4.
Private projects are on base-rate pass-through for commodities; government contracts use OEA/RBI-published indices, with escalation ranging from 6% to 30% across contracts.
Management is prioritising EPC and LSTK projects over item-rate work to raise revenue per worker, and will consider private projects above INR300-400 crores.
Order book is about 80-90% from Mumbai metro markets; management flagged Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities as more exposed to slowdown if costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: How are war and commodity prices affecting execution and profitability, and are contracts fixed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Private projects have 100% commodity pass-through, and government contracts have escalation, but indices lag actual prices for electrical and aluminium items. A INR10 crore provision was taken and will be reversed if escalation catches up over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth only 6% in Q4 and how much revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to labour migration around the West Bengal and BMC elections. It estimated about INR40-45 crores lost in Q4 and about INR125 crores for FY26, and said a tree-cutting permission delay on one IIT project also hurt revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 CIDCO, MHADA, NBCC and Signature Global revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CIDCO is seen at INR500-600 crores and MHADA at INR350-400 crores. Management did not give project-level figures for NBCC or Signature Global, and offered IR follow-up for top 5-6 projects. It also expects INR25-30 crores from Raymond.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost fell from 12.65% to 9.65% over 15 months after the rating upgrade to BBB+. FY27 finance cost is expected to fall by INR6-8 crores in absolute terms, and bank guarantee commissions have nearly halved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin downside if the war persists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.5% is the worst case on current inputs, but further rises in USD, fuel or commodities could hit EBITDA and PAT. It will update in Q1 or at the latest Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PSU/private split of the order book and the Q1 order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects PSU to stay around 50-60% of the order book and gave a quarterly inflow pipeline of about INR1,000 crores in Q1 and Q2, and INR2,500-3,000 crores in H2.

risks_watch: Escalation lag on electrical and aluminium inputs in government contracts; the INR10 crore provision reversal depends on escalation catching up in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Labour availability: about 3,000 workers short at 30 sites, with April execution affected and a 5% plus-or-minus recovery target by end-May.
Revenue growth of 6% in Q4 and 11-12% for FY26 versus earlier 18-20% expectations; FY27 20% guidance depends on execution pickup.
Other income fell sharply, from INR58 crores in FY25 to INR21 crores in FY26, reducing EBIT and PAT growth; management guides about INR3-4 crores per quarter going forward.
Non-core asset monetisation of about INR90 crores remaining over about 24 months, plus the INR50 crore FY27 target.
Management stated that NCR GRAP restrictions did not stop work from April to date, but environmental stoppages of 15-20 days are factored in.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet and cash metrics but cautious on near-term revenue and margins. Management repeatedly qualified guidance with the war and commodity uncertainty, and it was defensive when pressed on the Q4 growth shortfall and the earlier 18% growth claim.
